intro: Both forms are built on 限る, "to limit", and they point in opposite directions. に限らず ("not limited to X") takes X as one case and widens the statement to others as well. に限って ("limited to X") narrows the statement onto X, usually with irony: of all times or of all people, it happens with exactly X.

skills.rule: Noun + に限らず ... も: the statement is not limited to that noun; it is one case, and others are included too.
skills.explain:
に限らず is the written-style negative of 限る: "not limited to". It follows a noun and widens the statement beyond it. The second half names or implies the wider set, usually with も, 誰でも, どこでも or 多くの: この店は週末に限らず平日も混んでいる (the shop is busy not only at weekends but on weekdays too). The plain everyday equivalent is だけでなく.

The noun must be one member of a larger group: 子ども, 日本, 週末, 料理. That is the edge with を問わず and にかかわらず, which take a variable or an opposite pair (年齢, 性別, 天気, 経験の有無, 晴雨) and say it makes no difference. 子どもに限らず大人も楽しめる is "children, and adults too"; 年齢を問わず楽しめる is "whatever your age". 年齢に限らず is wrong, because age is not one member of a set.

はもちろん is close, but it adds that the first case is obvious. に限らず only says it is not the only one.
patterns: [noun] に限らず、どこでも / 誰でも [predicate]

examples.jp: 子[こ]ども{にかぎらず}、大人[おとな]もこのアニメが好[す]きです。
examples.en: Not only children but adults like this anime too.

examples.jp: この店[みせ]は週末[しゅうまつ]{にかぎらず}、平日[へいじつ]も混[こ]んでいます。
examples.en: This shop is crowded not only at weekends but on weekdays too.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]{にかぎらず}、多[おお]くの国[くに]で高齢化[こうれいか]が進[すす]んでいます。
examples.en: Not just in Japan: populations are ageing in many countries.

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]は東京[とうきょう]{にかぎらず}、どの大都市[だいとし]にもあります。
examples.en: This problem is not limited to Tokyo; every big city has it.

examples.jp: 料理[りょうり]{にかぎらず}、何[なに]をするにも練習[れんしゅう]が必要[ひつよう]です。
examples.en: Not just cooking: whatever you do, it takes practice.

contrast.note: を問わず takes a variable or a pair and says it does not matter: 年齢を問わず (whatever the age), 経験の有無を問わず (with or without experience). に限らず takes one member and adds the others: 学生に限らず社会人も.
Like を問わず, it cancels a varying condition: 天気にかかわらず (whatever the weather), 参加するしないにかかわらず. It cannot take a single member such as 学生 or 東京.
The opposite direction: に限って narrows onto X ("just when X", "X of all people"); に限らず spreads beyond X.

mistakes.bad: 年齢[ねんれい]{にかぎらず}、誰[だれ]でも参加[さんか]できます。
mistakes.good: 年齢[ねんれい]{をとわず}、誰[だれ]でも参加[さんか]できます。
mistakes.note: Age is a scale that varies, not one member of a group: "whatever your age" is を問わず.

mistakes.bad: 天気[てんき]{にかぎらず}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]われます。
mistakes.good: 天気[てんき]{にかかわらず}、試合[しあい]は行[おこな]われます。
mistakes.note: "Whatever the weather" cancels a condition: にかかわらず.

mistakes.bad: 学生[がくせい]{にかぎって}、社会人[しゃかいじん]も応募[おうぼ]できます。
mistakes.good: 学生[がくせい]{にかぎらず}、社会人[しゃかいじん]も応募[おうぼ]できます。
mistakes.note: Widening the group to working people needs the negative form, に限らず.

skills.tip: Add "and others too" after X. If it fits, に限らず. If X is a scale like age or weather ("whatever the X"), it is を問わず or にかかわらず.

skills.rule: X に限って + an unwelcome or unexpected fact: "just when X", "X of all people/times".
skills.explain:
に限って singles out one case and says that exactly there something happens that you would not expect or want. The typical frame is a plain-form clause + 時 / 日 + に限って, followed by a complaint: 急いでいる時に限って電車が遅れる (the train is always late just when I am in a hurry). It is the Japanese "just my luck".

With a person, often your own family or someone you trust, and a negative, it means "X, of all people, would never": うちの子に限ってそんなことはしない. The speaker defends X as the exception.

Plain limitation without irony is だけ in speech and に限り in notices: 本日に限り半額 (half price today only), 先着十名に限り. A neutral に限って (会員に限って入場できます) exists in formal writing, but in everyday sentences learners should not use it for a neutral habit: it adds the feeling that the coincidence is annoying or surprising.
patterns: [plain clause] 時 / 日 に限って [unwelcome event]
[trusted person] に限って [そんなことはない / するはずがない]

examples.jp: 忙[いそが]しい時[とき]{にかぎって}、電話[でんわ]がたくさんかかってくる。
examples.en: I get loads of calls just when I'm busy.

examples.jp: 急[いそ]いでいる時[とき]{にかぎって}、電車[でんしゃ]が遅[おく]れる。
examples.en: The train is always late precisely when I'm in a hurry.

examples.jp: 傘[かさ]を持[も]っていない日[ひ]{にかぎって}、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る。
examples.en: It always rains on the one day I don't have an umbrella.

examples.jp: 大事[だいじ]な試験[しけん]の前[まえ]{にかぎって}、風邪[かぜ]をひいてしまう。
examples.en: I always catch a cold right before an important exam.

examples.jp: うちの子[こ]{にかぎって}、そんなことをするはずがありません。
examples.en: My child, of all people, would never do something like that.

contrast.note: に限らず widens beyond X ("not only X"); に限って narrows onto X with irony. 子どもに限らず大人も is "adults too"; there is no widening in に限って.
に限り is the neutral limitation of signs and announcements: 本日に限り半額, 会員に限り入場できます. It carries no irony.
だけ limits neutrally: 雨の日だけ電車で行く (I take the train only on rainy days). 雨の日に限って電車が遅れる says the trains are late on exactly the days you need them.

mistakes.bad: 時間[じかん]がある時[とき]{にかぎって}、ゆっくり本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
mistakes.good: 時間[じかん]がある時[とき]{だけ}、ゆっくり本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
mistakes.note: A neutral habit restricted to some occasions is だけ; に限って would turn it into an annoying coincidence.

mistakes.bad: 子[こ]ども{にかぎって}、大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめます。
mistakes.good: 子[こ]ども{にかぎらず}、大人[おとな]も楽[たの]しめます。
mistakes.note: Adding adults to children widens the group: に限らず.

skills.tip: If "of all times" or "just my luck" fits the English, it is に限って.
